questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following in the correct order of their reactivity towards nucleophilic addition reactions
questions.solution: The reactivity of a substrate towards nucleophilic addition reactions depends on the groups attached to the carbonyl carbon that affect the charge density on it. III is most reactive due to absence of electron-donating $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ groups that are present on other compounds. II is least reactive due $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ and $-\mathrm{NH}_2$ that greatly increase the charge density on carbonyl carbon, making it least prone to nucleophilic attack. Among $\mathrm{I}$ and IV, I is more reactive due to only one $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ group. Thus, the order will be III > I > IV > II.

When propyne is treated with $dil{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ in presence of ${HgSO}_{4}$, the major product is acetone. A molecule of water is added to $C = C$ double bond to from an enol which tautomerizes to keto form.

${CH}_{3}C ≡ CH\overset{{HgSO}_{4}, {H}_{2}{SO}_{4}}{→}{CH}_{3}C\left(OH\right) = {CH}_{2}{CH}_{3}C\left(OH\right) = {CH}_{2}\overset{Tautomerises}{→}{CH}_{3}{COCH}_{3}$

The acetone formed in the above reaction, undergo aldol condensation reaction with barium hydroxide to give diacetone alcohol as shown below.

${CH}_{3}{COCH}_{3}\overset{Ba\left(OH\right)^{2}}{⇌}\left({CH}_{3}\right)2C\left(OH\right){CH}_{2}{COCH}_{3}\left({CH}_{3}\right)2C\left(OH\right){CH}_{2}{COCH}_{3}\mathop{→}_{- {H}_{2}O}^{∆}\left({CH}_{3}\right)2C = {CHCOCH}_{3}$

The molecular formula of diacetone alcohol formed is ${C}_{6}{H}_{10}O$.

$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COCl} \stackrel{\mathrm{Pd} / \mathrm{BaSO}_4}{\stackrel{\mathrm{H}_2}{\longrightarrow}} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHO}+\mathrm{HCl}$
